cause.what_happened: CTEV gapped from 31.62 to 28.82 at the open (per the sealed baseline and Yahoo's bars) and slid about 10.7% more intraday to 25.74 by 15:04 ET on below-normal volume. There was no 8-K, no press release and no filing on the day. Over the same days at least 20 new provider antitrust complaints naming MultiPlan were filed in N.D. Illinois (09-21 to 09-23), up from about 32 in the ten weeks before 09-09. That is the only dated adverse item I found and I cannot show that it caused the fall. The slide has been continuous since the 09-15 Morgan Stanley conference (36.44 on 09-14, 30.81 on 09-18).

findings.finding: Provider antitrust complaints against MultiPlan/Claritev are hitting N.D. Illinois dockets at several a day: 5 or more on 09-21, 9 on 09-22 and 6 on 09-23, against about 32 in the previous ten weeks. The pattern is likely to continue on 09-24 and keep the litigation overhang visible.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The wave is running daily right now (09-21, 09-22, 09-23), so further complaints docketed on 09-24 land inside the window. Each one is public on PACER/CourtListener the same day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Legal and regulatory news has moved this stock hard before: -15% on 2026-05-14 when the DOJ criminal probe was reported, and -8.5% on 2026-07-14 when the civil probe was expanded (gurufocus). Those were DOJ headlines, though, not individual provider complaints. Complaints have been added to MDL 3121 all summer without any dated price reaction that I could find.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has taken the complaints already on the docket. What it may not have taken is that the filing rate is accelerating with no stated end date. If the market had fully priced a continuing wave, I would expect to see a finished cause, such as a deadline that has passed or a settlement, and I found neither. Individual complaints are low-visibility, though, so most of this is probably already in the price or irrelevant to it. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: none. The GCR (2026-07-16) and Capitol Forum reports cover the DOJ side, not this wave: https://globalcompetitionreview.com/gcr-usa/article/doj-deepens-claritev-probe-massive-info-request

baseline_tension: Mostly consistent. The name's own falls (median -1.59, 37.5% up), ATR 10.1% and the downside-paid skew all lean toward continuation. The below-normal volume (0.91x) and the lack of any named cause lean toward the under-2x bounce cohort. A possible two-day merge in the baseline would put this fall in a milder band.
